summary.headline: Gravita Q2 FY27 revenue rose 38% YoY to INR1,427 crore, but lead volumes fell on scrap shortages from the Gulf disruption.
summary.overview: Management described a resilient Q2 and H1 FY27, with H1 revenue, EBITDA and PAT up 40%, 29% and 10% respectively. Total volume rose 3% YoY to 52,199 MTPA, though lead volumes were weak (down about 11% YoY) because scrap flows from the Gulf and other territories were disrupted. Copper profitability improved sharply after the RMIL consolidation, with copper EBITDA per ton at INR84,671 in Q2. Management guided to a recovery in lead volumes from Q3 as new overseas yards and domestic reverse-charge procurement ramp up.

financial_highlights.metric: H1 FY27 revenue / EBITDA / PAT growth

financial_highlights.value: Lead INR22,620; Aluminium INR22,664; Plastic INR10,334; Copper INR84,671
INR18 crore total (INR9.39 crore operational, INR8.61 crore non-operational)

segments.name: Lead
segments.commentary: Volumes were the weakest in several quarters, down about 11% YoY and QoQ, due to raw material availability; EBITDA per ton was INR22,620 in Q2. Management guided to 18-20% volume CAGR over the next three years.

segments.name: Aluminium
segments.commentary: EBITDA per ton was INR22,664 in Q2. Sourcing is mainly local African scrap across four locations; the Jaipur unit is being shifted to Mundra.

segments.name: Plastics
segments.commentary: Segment reported strong growth momentum in Q2 with sustained demand; EBITDA per ton was INR10,334.

segments.name: Copper (incl. RMIL)
segments.commentary: Operated at 50% capacity utilisation in H1 with sales up 12%; EBITDA per ton of INR84,671 in Q2. RMIL contributed INR420 crore revenue at an 8.5% EBITDA margin, and RMIL's utilisation is seen rising to 65-70% in 2-3 quarters.

guidance_outlook: Copper sustainable EBITDA of INR65-70 per kg for the next few quarters, rising to INR80-90 per kg in 2-3 years after backward integration; the Q2 figure was boosted by a sales mix and high-value orders.
Lead volumes expected to improve from Q3 FY27 as overseas yards and domestic reverse-charge procurement start contributing.
Lead volume growth targeted at 18-20% a year over three years, with some quarters likely to fall short.
Scrap sourcing mix for India targeted at 40-50% domestic and 50-60% overseas (Q2 mix was 26% domestic battery scrap, 74% imported).
Total capex of INR1,680 crore through FY29, of which INR815 crore goes to existing businesses; about INR600-680 crore already spent. Capacity is planned to rise from about 480,000 to 800,000 tons.
Mandvi copper plant (29,400 MTPA, about INR160 crore) on track for commissioning within 12 months; Mundra copper expansion (59,200 MTPA, about INR64 crore) to be commissioned in phases by March 2029.
capex_capacity: Mundra: 59,200 MTPA copper recycling capacity, about INR64 crore, internally funded, phased commissioning by March 2029.
Mandvi, Gujarat: 29,400 MTPA copper recycling facility, about INR160 crore, internally funded, commissioning within 12 months.

RMIL: approved about INR94.42 crore investment in its rights issue (total issue about INR94.81 crore). Bottlenecks need debottlenecking now (2-3 quarters to reach 65-70% utilisation); a capacity increase would take about 3 years.
Total capex INR1,680 crore through FY29; capacity to rise from about 480,000 to 800,000 tons.
Gravita Recyclers USA, Inc. incorporated with initial capital of US$50,000 to build a US scrap sourcing network; yards are to be leased, so capex is minimal and working capital is the main need.
demand_pricing: Management said demand is not the issue; the Q2 lead volume shortfall was caused by raw material availability after the Gulf-related supply disruption.
Copper scrap is largely sourced from the US via aggregators; Gravita plans its own yards to earn an estimated 2-3% extra margin.
Copper is fully hedged; lead is hedged. Aluminium cannot be hedged because it is not traded.
Reverse-charge mechanism on e-waste and battery scrap is expected to bring domestic volumes and level the playing field with the unorganised sector, which had an 18% margin advantage from GST.
EPR credit prices are cited at INR5.40-18 per kg; credit demand is expected to surge after the 7-year BWMR window closes.

qa_highlights.question: How much has the West Asia crisis affected scrap sourcing and exports, and is the impact easing?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said new geographies are being developed, with some material arriving from Q3 and bookings started in Q2. It also said the worst is over, citing reverse-charge demand domestically.

qa_highlights.question: Is the lead volume drop a one-off, and what is the outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Lead working capital cycle is 80-90 days, so new bookings take about 90 days to arrive. Management called Q2 a one-off quarter and expects growth to return.

qa_highlights.question: What is sustainable copper EBITDA per ton?
qa_highlights.answer: Sustainable copper EBITDA is INR65-70 per kg in the near term, rising to INR80-90 per kg in 2-3 years. Q2 was boosted by sales and raw material mix, higher utilisation and some high-value orders.

qa_highlights.question: Why did standalone PAT fall about 50% while consolidated PAT rose 6%?
qa_highlights.answer: The increase came mainly from RMIL (copper) and overseas subsidiaries.

qa_highlights.question: What is the copper sourcing plan and the US subsidiary's role?
qa_highlights.answer: The US subsidiary is a sourcing arm with no direct revenue. It will run its own yards, feeding copper and battery scrap to India. Capex is limited because yards are leased.

qa_highlights.question: Will lower-cost US sourcing hurt lead EBITDA per kg, and would lead capex be delayed?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said US scrap may cost more than Africa, but it still meets internal ROCE targets. Capex will not be delayed while scrap is available for the next 3-4 years.

risks_watch: Lead volume recovery depends on overseas yard ramp-up and domestic reverse-charge notification, which is not yet notified.
Copper EBITDA of about INR84,671 per ton in Q2 includes one-off high-value orders; management guides to a lower INR65-70 per kg run rate.
RMIL utilisation is stagnant; reaching 65-70% depends on debottlenecking and new machinery orders.
EU waste-shipment restrictions could limit aluminium scrap availability; India is negotiating with the EU.
Import policy changes on scrap or tyres (TPO) could affect sourcing and fuel cost.
summary.management_tone: Confident on long-term recovery and the copper build-out, but candid that lead volumes were hit by raw material shortages. Answers were direct on margins and capex, and vaguer on timing for the lead recovery and the US yard rollout.
key_quotes: So we are very confident that we'll turn around this issue in the next couple of quarters.
So overall, capex, we are pretty much in line with the 2030 plan.
So the only constraint in future is going to be the scrap availability.

adds.what: Capacity rising from ~480,000 to 800,000 tons by FY29 (total capex INR1,680 crore)

growth.why: Management guides lead volume CAGR of 18-20% over three years and copper capacity rising from ~480,000 to 800,000 tons by FY29 on INR1,680 crore capex, with Mundra and Mandvi copper plants (~88,600 MTPA combined) and RMIL utilisation rising to 65-70% in 2-3 quarters; Q2 lead volumes were down ~11% YoY, so near-term delivery is only partly evidenced.
